R1061.note: Allowlists sort column against SELECT columns and direction against ASC/DESC, falling back to safe defaults; matches stated contract exactly.

R1062.note: Moves the route from apiMux to protectedMux; handler logic (202/405 responses) untouched, matching contract.

R1063.note: Closes the shell injection, but silently swaps ICMP ping diagnostics for a TCP connect on port 80, changing what 'reachable' means (loses latency/packet-loss, fails hosts with port 80 closed) while the write-up claims it 'performs the same network reachability goal'.

R1064.note: Removes the stray [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken]; endpoint reverts to the app-wide antiforgery filter as intended.

R1065.note: Null check placed before strcmp, matches contract exactly.

R1066.note: Winston meta object is JSON-stringified by the simple() format, escaping control characters and neutralizing log-line forging.

R1067.note: Removing BinaryFormatter is the only real fix for this sink, but the wire format silently changes from binary to JSON; a legitimate client sending a real serialized session blob will now get an unhandled parse exception, and this compatibility break is never flagged.

R1068.note: AST allowlist evaluator restricts to constants/names/binary-unary arithmetic and rejects unknown names, matching the stated contract.

R1069.note: Converts to a proper parameterized StoredProcedure call; customerId is always bound as data.

R1070.note: Adds the missing %255s width and validates the source is NUL-terminated via strnlen before scanning; matches the vulnerable pattern exactly.

R1071.note: Replaces exec() with the whois npm package, eliminating the shell entirely while preserving the lookup/response behavior.

R1072.note: Switches to the Runtime.exec(String[]) array form, removing shell interpretation; residual flag-injection risk is explicitly flagged as an optional secondary hardening step, not silently left.

R1073.note: Deny-by-default JexlSandbox blocks reflection/class access while leaving built-in comparison/arithmetic on the primitive context variables (amount, region, owner) functional for the stated common filters.

R1074.note: Adds a straightforward bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write; matches the vulnerable code exactly.

R1075.note: Allowlist of sort columns matches the SELECT clause; bound params for account_id/status untouched.

R1076.note: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') is a standard CSPRNG token replacement; format/lifespan otherwise unchanged.

R1077.note: Adds bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the read; matches the vulnerable code exactly.

R1078.note: Case explicitly warns the fix must patch LookupRate's file-read (via allowlist/dict) while preserving arbitrary rule-expression evaluation with orderTotal arithmetic; instead this deletes DynamicExpresso entirely and only accepts three hardcoded literal rule strings, silently breaking any legitimate rule expression while presenting it as equivalent.

R1079.note: Captures the fd value at enqueue time instead of the Connection pointer, removing the dangling-pointer dependency entirely; minimal and correct.

R1080.note: Adds secure:true (the actual finding) plus sameSite:'lax' as a disclosed, non-breaking defense-in-depth addition for this same-site SSO redirect flow.

R1081.note: Reference-counts the Connection (init refcount=1, addref on capture, decrement-then-free on release) so the shared owner and the queued callback correctly coordinate the free; traced through and consistent.

R1082.note: Adds @csrf_protect from starlette_wtf matching the sibling update_profile_note route exactly; correct and minimal.

R1083.note: Replaces the string-eval'd assert() with a direct boolean assert(); the assert()-throws-on-false gating behavior is preserved identically since the original code never checked assert()'s return value either.

R1084.note: OWASP Encoder Encode.forHtml() applied at both interpolation points is the correct context-aware fix; write-up doesn't mention adding the new dependency to the build file, a minor omission.

R1085.note: crypto.randomBytes(16) base64url is a valid CSPRNG token replacement, URL-safe like the original.

R1086.note: Adds can:update,order matching the exact pattern already used by the sibling update/cancel routes per the case's own description.

R1087.note: Fully replaces PowerShell/Process.Start with System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping, removing the shell entirely; output format change is openly shown in the full rewritten handler, not hidden.

R1088.note: Converts to JNDI parameterized filter args ({0}/{1}) which RFC-4515-escape both param and the hardcoded street value; correct and minimal.

R1089.note: html.escape() applied to all three interpolated values; standard, correct, minimal.

R1090.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) does stop the OOB read, but for an unterminated name it silently returns 16 and the caller treats that as a normal valid length rather than failing closed/flagging invalid data, which is exactly the trap this case was built to catch given the stated contract.

R1091.note: Moves the f-string-interpolated date into a bound :date_filter parameter; correct and minimal.

R1092.note: Standard sqlite3 ? placeholder parameterization; matches contract, client-side escaping correctly left untouched.

R1098.note: archive/tar replacement correctly removes the shell sink and preserves the 400/500/text-plain behaviors, but the ctx parameter is no longer used anywhere in the rewritten body, silently dropping the request-context cancellation support the stated contract explicitly requires to be kept.

R1099.note: The overall magic-byte validation approach and preserved response/extension behavior are correct, but Image.TryIdentifyFormat(stream, out format) does not appear to be a real SixLabors.ImageSharp API (the library exposes Image.Identify/DetectFormat instead), risking a build failure as written.

R1100.note: System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(Model.Label) embeds a JSON string literal directly in the script; .NET's default JavaScriptEncoder escapes HTML-sensitive characters (</script> etc.), so this is safe for the script context and preserves refreshSeconds as a number.
